about.title: Vernon Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Vernon runs almost entirely on industry, from meatpacking and food processing to logistics yards packed along Santa Fe Avenue and S Soto Street. That density means forklifts, loading docks, delivery trucks, and heavy machinery are part of daily work life, and injuries happen more often than most people expect. In California, workers' comp usually covers medical care and lost wages regardless of fault, but it doesn't account for pain and suffering. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may also have a separate third-party claim outside the workers' comp system. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves, we're a free service that connects injured workers in Vernon with an independent attorney who can sort out which path, or paths, apply to your situation. There's no cost unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Vernon Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Help Identify Third-Party Claims
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually your only claim against an employer, but a negligent contractor, driver, or equipment maker can open a separate injury case. An attorney can review your accident to see if that applies.

items.title: We Understand the Reporting Clock
items.desc: California requires you report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate a claim. We connect you quickly so an attorney can help you protect your rights early.

items.title: We Know Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: Employers can't legally punish you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you're worried about your job, an independent attorney can advise you on what protections apply in your situation.

items.question: I was hurt at a warehouse in Vernon. Can I still get workers' comp if it was partly my fault?
items.answer: Yes, in most cases. California workers' comp generally doesn't require proving fault, so it typically applies even if you made a mistake on the job. There are exceptions, like intoxication or intentional self-harm, so it helps to have an attorney review the specifics.

items.question: What if a delivery truck hit me while I was working near Santa Fe Avenue or District Boulevard?
items.answer: That could involve both a workers' comp claim and a separate third-party claim against the driver or their employer. Vernon's industrial corridors see steady vehicle and pedestrian traffic, and a collision caused by someone outside your own employer generally isn't limited by the workers' comp exclusivity rule. An attorney can help sort out which claims apply and the two-year deadline for the third-party portion.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a workplace injury in Vernon?
items.answer: You generally need to report the injury to your employer within 30 days to preserve your workers' comp rights. If a third party was involved, that separate claim usually carries a two-year deadline under California law. Because these timelines run differently, it's worth speaking with an attorney sooner rather than later.
